# Chess report for ashton-iwnl

You're scoring about what your rating predicts: 51% against an expected 49% over 300 games [F1]. Your blunder rate is normal for your level, at 0.98 times the expected count [F2], so none of your results show a clear weakness.

## Biggest weaknesses

No opening family shows a weakness that is clear once opponent rating, sample size and the number of openings checked are taken into account [F9]. One area is worth watching:

1. **Scotch Game as Black (thin evidence).** You scored 21% here against 46% expected, across only 12 games [F8]. With 34 openings checked, one result this extreme is expected by luck alone [F8]. In moves 13-25 of these games you lost 6.2 win% per move, against 5.1 across all your games [F15]. Your losses include a Goring Gambit Declined line with 4.c3 d5 and a Scotch Gambit line with 4.Bc4 d6 [T1]. That Scotch Gambit game also contains your most costly move: 43...Kh7 lost 93 win% when Qxf4+ was available [F16]. **What to do:** pick one solid answer each to 4.c3 and 4.Bc4, and replay these three games [T1] to see where the early middlegame went wrong.

## What's working

- **Queen's Gambit as White:** you scored 60% against 50% expected over 48 games [F6], with a median eval of +1.0 pawns after move 12 [F13]. Your preparation is getting you good positions.
- **Handling time pressure:** with under 10% of your clock left you made 0.89 times the expected number of blunders [F3]. With 10-30% left it was 0.84 times expected [F4]. You hold up well in time trouble.

## Training plan

- When you have plenty of time, slow down and check for checks. Most of your blunders come with over 30% of the clock left: 421 of them, at 1.02 times expected [F5]. For example, 38...Qh2+ lost 88 win% when Bf6 was better [F18].
- Do middlegame puzzles: https://lichess.org/training/middlegame [F19]. Your middlegame blunder rate is 6.6% [F11], the highest of the three phases. It matches your opponents' rate, so this is about gaining an edge rather than fixing a flaw.
- Do hanging-piece puzzles: https://lichess.org/training/hangingPiece [F20]. 7...h5 missed Nxg4 and cost 89 win% [F17].
- Learn one repertoire line against the Scotch and its gambits, and review your losses with it [T1].
- Keep playing the Queen's Gambit, and look over your moves 13-25 in it, where you lose 5.2 win% per move [F13].
